references.text: Moses' song speaks of the day of vengeance: "Vengeance is mine, I will repay" ([ref:5 Mos 32:35|Deuteronomy 32:35]). Jesus links the destruction of Jerusalem to the fulfillment of God's righteous judgment, as Moses foretold.

Isaiah prophesies about "a day of vengeance for the Lord, a year of recompense" ([ref:Jes 34:8|Isaiah 34:8]). Luke 21:22 uses the phrase "days of vengeance" (ἡμέραι ἐκδικήσεως) in line with this prophetic tradition concerning God's judgment.

Isaiah 61:2 mentions "a day of vengeance from our God" ([ref:Jes 61:2|Isaiah 61:2]). Jesus read from this passage in Nazareth (Luke 4:18–19) but stopped before the day of vengeance – in Luke 21:22 he warns that this part is now to be fulfilled.

Hosea says, "The days of punishment have come, the days of recompense have come" ([ref:Hos 9:7|Hosea 9:7]). The phrase is closely related to Jesus' words about "days of vengeance" and concerns judgment upon an unfaithful people.

Jeremiah asks whether the Lord should not punish a people like this ([ref:Jer 5:29|Jeremiah 5:29]). The idea that God's judgment ultimately falls on a rebellious people is the same as in Jesus' warning about the destruction of Jerusalem.

Jeremiah speaks of "a day of vengeance" when the Lord takes vengeance on his enemies ([ref:Jer 46:10|Jeremiah 46:10]). Jesus uses the same motif in his eschatological discourse concerning the fall of Jerusalem.

Daniel prophesies that the city and the sanctuary will be destroyed ([ref:Dan 9:26|Daniel 9:26]). Jesus' words that everything written must be fulfilled include Daniel's prophecy about the destruction of Jerusalem.

Daniel speaks of a time when all these things will be accomplished ([ref:Dan 12:7|Daniel 12:7]). Jesus' expression "so that all that is written may be fulfilled" (τοῦ πλησθῆναι πάντα τὰ γεγραμμένα) points to the fulfillment of such prophecies.

Jesus promises that God will "bring swift justice for his chosen ones" ([ref:Luk 18:7-8|Luke 18:7–8]). The word ἐκδίκησις (vengeance/justice) is used here in the same way as in Luke 21:22, linking God's righteous intervention to the end times.

Jesus weeps over Jerusalem and predicts that enemies will surround the city and level it to the ground, "because you did not know the time of your visitation" ([ref:Luk 19:43-44|Luke 19:43–44]). This is a parallel prophecy concerning the same judgment described in Luke 21:22.
